# Lean `ServeEntry` modes allowed to have no caller (#1003).
#
#     mode<TAB>kind<TAB>reason
#
# Checked by `cargo run --example mode_reachability`, which reads the dispatch
# arms out of `lean/ServeEntry.lean` and the run's execution trace, and holds
# THIS FILE EXACT in both directions: a mode here that has gained a caller
# fails, and a mode here that the table no longer dispatches fails. So it
# cannot rot quietly, which is the only reason a list like this is safe to
# have at all.
#
# `ablation`  Exists to be subtracted from a real mode, to separate what the
#             verified core costs from what the crossing costs. A caller is a
#             DEFECT here: it means something in the tree is treating an empty
#             reply as an answer.
#
# `bless`     Runs only under a bless env var, which a gate must never set --
#             blessing rewrites the oracle the gate judges against. A caller in
#             a gate run is a DEFECT for that reason, not for the ablation one.
#
# `dead`      Has no caller and should have one. Grandfathered, and it
#             RATCHETS DOWN in the same discipline as `.dev-lint-baseline`:
#             giving one of these a caller means deleting its line, and the
#             check will insist on it. Nothing may be ADDED here without the
#             reason saying why the mode cannot be exercised yet — the check
#             cannot tell a new orphan from an old one, and that part is a
#             review question.
#
# ⚠ `lean_serve` is NOT a caller for this purpose. It is the hop-1 probe: it
# asks modes a question purely to show `dispatch` still routes to them. See
# `PROBES` in the checker.

# ── by design: a caller here is a defect ──────────────────────────────────────

noop	ablation	#405's floor: accept the request, do nothing, reply empty. `real - noop` is what consulting Lean costs at all.
echo	ablation	The response half of the same floor -- ships the input rows back so a real-sized reply crosses with no work behind it.
gqdecode	ablation	Layer 3 for gpsquality: runs its parse and stops, so `real - gqdecode` is the filter plus its encode.
daydecode	ablation	Layer 3 for the day mode (#433), the counterpart of gqdecode.
dayresp	ablation	Layer 2 for the day mode (#433): the chain with no row encoding.
ceilingbless	bless	feasibility_corpus:278 reaches it only under FEASIBILITY_BLESS. A gate run that got here would be rewriting the ceiling it is judged against.

# ── dead: these want a caller, and this list ratchets DOWN ────────────────────

railsnap	dead	HAS a production caller -- lean::rail_snap, main.rs:4696 -- that no test exercises, so the arm is live in prod and unexercised by every gate. Different from the rest of this section: wanted here is a TEST, not a caller.
assemble	dead	No caller. Verified.Hsmm.Assemble is dispatched and has never decoded a production day (#1003's own standing note).
assembledecode	dead	No caller through dispatch. cliMain reaches assembleDecodeResult straight from argv, which does not route through the table, so the ARM is dead while the handler is not.
coverage	dead	No caller through dispatch. Same argv shape as assembledecode. The backend's own `coverage` CLI subcommand (lib.rs:101) is an unrelated name.
geo	dead	No caller through dispatch; cliMain reaches geoMain from argv.
match	dead	No caller through dispatch; cliMain reaches matchMain from argv.
rail	dead	No caller through dispatch; cliMain reaches railMain from argv. The `rail` in main.rs:5972 is a mirror TABLE name, not this mode.
hsmm	dead	No caller anywhere, argv included.

# ── found by this check on its first run, 2026-09-05 ──────────────────────────
# All three were traced ONLY by `lean_serve`, the hop-1 probe. Every check we
# had called them green; that is the gap #1003 describes, measured.

focus	dead	HAS a production caller -- the focus-places cron, main.rs:3945 -- and no test. Same shape as railsnap: live in prod, unexercised by every gate. Wanted here is a TEST.
biolabels	dead	No caller at all. #1003 listed it "test/example only"; measured, its only caller is the routing probe.
stationchain	dead	No caller at all. #1003 listed it "test/example only"; measured, its only caller is the routing probe.
